verdicts.quote: A first reminder becomes eligible on the calendar day after the invoice due date. ... Observe no first reminder on the due date or earlier
An invoice with a zero or negative balance is ineligible at delivery handoff. ... Settle the invoice or apply a credit covering the amount owed
verdicts.missing: Whether disputed invoices or invoices on a payment plan stop the sequence; paid, credited, voided (C-22) and part-paid (continues, U-5) are addressed but disputes and payment plans are not.

verdicts.quote: A reminder shows the invoice's remaining balance in its currency. Observable: Apply a partial payment before sending and observe the remaining amount shown
Existing recipient restrictions for billing communications apply to reminders.
verdicts.missing: Whether a reminder, as a billing notice, is exempt from a marketing opt-out/unsubscribe, and how paused customer states are treated.

verdicts.quote: Repeated or concurrent evaluations do not duplicate a delivery handoff for the same reminder opportunity.
An invoice with a zero or negative balance is ineligible at delivery handoff.
A temporarily rejected reminder is retried if the invoice remains eligible.
verdicts.missing: Behaviour during a prolonged provider outage, any limit on retries, and escalation to a person when delivery keeps failing.

verdicts.quote: Reminder handoffs honor the delivery service's applicable sending limit. ... observe that handoffs stay within that limit.
Missed reminder dates do not accumulate separate catch-up sends.
verdicts.missing: Whether the backlog of already-overdue invoices across the account is staggered on activation; C-25 has all of them considered on the next evaluation, limited only by the delivery limit.

verdicts.quote: Reminder calendar dates use the account's billing time zone when one is set.
verdicts.missing: Sending hours, business hours, and weekend/holiday handling; C-19 explicitly avoids an exact send time.

verdicts.quote: A reminder shows the invoice's remaining balance in its currency.
verdicts.missing: How the amount and currency are formatted for the recipient (locale, symbol, decimals).

verdicts.quote: Evaluate an otherwise eligible invoice with no designated billing email or an invalid address and observe no reminder for that invoice.
A reminder is sent to the invoice's designated billing recipient.
verdicts.missing: What happens when there are several billing contacts: whether all, one, or which one is written to.

verdicts.quote: An authorized billing operator can distinguish delivery outcomes for an affected invoice.
verdicts.missing: A per-invoice, per-reminder-step record of what was sent and when, visible on the invoice.

verdicts.quote: A reminder provides access to the invoice's existing way to pay where one exists.
verdicts.missing: Whether the reminder shows the due date and whether the payment link expires; reference (C-12) and amount (C-13) are stated.

verdicts.quote: An unauthorized reminder setting change is refused.
verdicts.missing: Who may stop an individual invoice's reminder by hand; manual sending is deferred to existing rules (C-57) and the schedule itself is not configurable.

verdicts.quote: An authorized billing operator can disable reminders for their billing account.
verdicts.missing: A global off switch beyond per-account disable, per-customer turn-off, and any preview or dry run; manual resend is only deferred to existing rules (C-57).

verdicts.quote: Inspect reminders with accepted, temporarily rejected, permanently rejected, and uncertain handoffs and observe which outcome applies to each.
verdicts.missing: A view of which reminders the system will send next.

verdicts.quote: Reminder handoffs honor the delivery service's applicable sending limit.
Invoice payments follow their existing rules.
